findings.description: F-015: the R shortcut matched Latin keysyms only, so it was dead under a Russian keyboard layout although the button is labelled 'Новый раунд (R)'.
findings.resolution: Extended on_key in tic_tac_toe.py to accept ('r', 'R', 'Cyrillic_ka', 'Cyrillic_KA') with a comment noting digits are layout-independent but the letter is not. Verified: driving on_key with keysym='Cyrillic_ka' now resets the board (previously it did not).

evidence.summary: Learning objective and scope: Routes keyboard input into the same attempt_move() that mouse clicks use, so the game's rules exist in exactly one place, and maps keys 1-9 to cell indices 0-8.

Keys 1-9 map to indices 0-8 via attempt_move(n - 1), and the keyboard handler contains no rules of its own. -- confirmed -- driving the real app's on_key with char='3' places a mark at board[2]; char='0' is correctly ignored; all nine mappings match the printed table.

Both the mouse path and the keyboard path converge on one function, so the rules are not duplicated. -- confirmed -- tic_tac_toe.py's command= binding and on_key both call self.attempt_move(...), and neither contains a win/draw check of its own.

event.char is the actual character typed, predictable for the top-row digits, but NumPad behaviour can vary with platform, layout and NumLock. -- confirmed and appropriately hedged -- event_generate('<Key>', keysym='3') delivers keysym='3' and char='3' on this build; the NumPad caveat is a correct statement of a genuinely platform-dependent area.

Pressing R starts a new round. -- CONFIRMED ONLY FOR A LATIN LAYOUT as found -- on_key matched event.keysym in ('r','R') only, so keysym='Cyrillic_ka'/char='к' (the physical R key on a Russian layout) did NOT reset the board. Fixed under F-015; digits 1-9 are layout-independent and were unaffected.
